title: Battery safety
rules: Tape both terminals of every used battery (or put each in its own small bag) so they cannot short-circuit.
Store used batteries in a dry glass jar or cardboard box, away from heat and metal objects.
Take them to a battery collection box; many supermarkets and electronics stores have one.
Treat swollen, leaking or hot lithium batteries as urgent: put them on sand or a ceramic plate outdoors and drop them off quickly.
never: Never put batteries in the household bin or recycling bin: they cause fires in waste trucks.
Never burn, crush, puncture or open a battery.
Never try to recharge single-use alkaline batteries.

title: Electronics and e-waste safety
rules: Back up and erase personal data, then factory-reset phones, tablets and computers before handing them in.
Keep devices whole: the collection point removes batteries and parts safely.
Tape over cracked screens so glass fragments stay in place.
Hand devices to an e-waste collection point, a retailer take-back box or a certified refurbisher.
never: Never open or dismantle devices with built-in lithium batteries at home.
Never put electronics, cables or chargers in household bins.
Never burn cables to recover copper.

title: Chemical containers
rules: Keep chemicals in their original labelled containers with the lids tightly closed.
Take leftover paint, solvents, pesticides, strong cleaners and motor oil to a hazardous waste collection point.
Transport containers upright in a box, separated from each other.
never: Never reuse a container that held chemicals, pesticides, solvents or motor oil for food, drink, edible plants or pets.
Never mix chemicals: bleach and ammonia or acids together release toxic gas.
Never pour chemicals down drains, into the sand or into the sea.

title: Aerosol can safety
rules: Use the can until it is completely empty and no longer hisses when pressed.
Keep the cap on and store it upright, out of the sun.
Take cans that are not empty, or held paint, solvent or insecticide, to hazardous waste collection.
never: Never puncture, crush, cut or burn an aerosol can, even when it seems empty.
Never leave aerosols in a hot car or in direct UAE summer sun: they can burst.
Never reuse an aerosol can for crafts.

title: Medicine disposal
rules: Take expired or unused medicines, including blister packs with tablets left, back to a pharmacy and ask how they collect them.
Keep medicines in their original packaging so they can be identified.
Cross out your name on labels before handing them in.
Empty blister packs with no tablets left can go to general waste.
never: Never flush medicines down the toilet or sink.
Never give prescription medicines to someone else.
Never reuse medicine bottles or blister packs for crafts children could mistake for sweets.

title: Light bulbs and fluorescent tubes
rules: Energy-saving CFL bulbs and fluorescent tubes contain a small amount of mercury: take them to a hazardous waste or lamp collection point.
LED bulbs contain electronics and go to e-waste collection.
Old incandescent and halogen bulbs are not glass-bank glass: wrap them and follow local collection advice.
Keep bulbs in their original box or wrapped in paper until drop-off.
never: Never put bulbs in the glass recycling bank.
Never break a bulb on purpose or use one for crafts.
If a CFL breaks, never vacuum it: air the room for 15 minutes, scoop the pieces with card and seal them in a jar.

title: Broken glass disposal
rules: Put on thick gloves and pick up large pieces first, then press sticky tape or a slice of bread on small splinters.
Wrap the pieces in several sheets of newspaper or put them in a rigid box or jar and tape it shut.
Label the package 'broken glass' so collection staff are warned.
Broken jars and bottles can go in the glass bank only if the bank accepts them loose; otherwise use general waste in a sealed box.
never: Never pick up splinters with bare hands.
Never put loose broken glass in a plastic bag.
Never use broken glass for DIY projects.

title: Glass safety
rules: Check jars and bottles for chips and hairline cracks before using them; cracked glass can shatter when heated or pressed.
Wear work gloves and safety glasses if you drill, sand or cut glass, and keep the glass wet while drilling.
Put glass on a towel or non-slip mat while you work so it cannot roll.
Let glass cool fully after hot water or a candle before touching it.
never: Never pour boiling water into a cold jar.
Never cut glass bottles with string and fire.
Never use chipped glass for food or drink.

title: Cutting safely
rules: Cut on a cutting mat or thick board, never on your lap or hand.
Always cut away from your body and keep your other hand behind the blade.
Wear work gloves when using a craft knife, and use several light passes instead of one hard cut.
Retract or cap the blade and put it away as soon as you finish.
never: Never use a dull blade: it slips. Snap off or replace it.
Never leave blades where children can reach them.

title: Sanding safely
rules: Wear a dust mask; add safety glasses when sanding overhead or with a power sander.
Sand outdoors or with a window open and wipe dust with a damp cloth instead of sweeping it into the air.
Work from coarse to fine sandpaper and sand along the grain.
never: Never dry-sand old paint that may contain lead: seal it instead.
Never sand pressure-treated or MB-stamped wood.

title: Drilling safely
rules: Wear safety glasses and tie back long hair and loose sleeves.
Clamp the piece; never hold small parts in your hand while drilling.
Drill a small pilot hole first and let the drill do the work.
Check walls for pipes and cables before drilling into them.
never: Never wear gloves near a spinning bit: they can catch and pull your hand in.
Never drill a sealed can or anything that held fuel or aerosol.

title: Painting, spraying and sealing
rules: Wear gloves or old clothes and cover your work surface.
Spray paint and varnish outdoors or by an open window, and wear a dust mask for spray paint.
Keep painted surfaces away from food unless the finish is labelled food-safe; paint the outside of containers only.
Let each coat dry fully and close tins tightly.
never: Never spray near a flame, stove or cigarette.
Never pour leftover paint or thinner down the drain.

title: Candles and heat
rules: Prefer LED tea lights indoors, near fabric or where children play.
Put real candles only in glass or metal holders on a heat-proof surface, 30 cm below anything that can burn.
Lift hot metal lanterns by the handle only.
never: Never leave a burning candle unattended.
Never put a candle inside plastic, paper or fabric.
Never heat, melt or burn plastic: the fumes are toxic.

title: Cans and sharp metal
rules: Wear work gloves when cutting, punching or handling opened cans.
File or sand cut edges, or cover them with tape, before anyone uses the object.
Punch holes with the can on a wooden board; filling it with frozen water stops it from denting.
never: Never cut or punch aerosol cans or anything that held fuel.
Never leave sharp strips of metal loose: fold the edges back.

title: Mold
rules: Items with visible mold are not suitable for donation or crafts.
Bag moldy textiles, paper and wood outdoors and put them in general waste.
Wash your hands after handling them.
never: Never shake moldy items indoors: spores spread.
Never put moldy textiles in clothing donation or recycling bins.

title: Never heat plastic
rules: Shape and join plastic cold: cut, fold, lace, weave, glue or screw it.
Use LED lights, never flames, inside plastic lamps and lanterns.
Keep plastic projects out of direct summer sun for long periods; heat warps them.
never: Never melt, burn, iron or bake plastic, and never heat nails to pierce it: the fumes are toxic.
Never microwave plastic that is not labelled microwave-safe.

title: Food contact after upcycling
rules: Only containers that originally held food should be reused for food, and only if they are intact and clean.
Painted or varnished surfaces must not touch food unless the product is labelled food-safe; paint the outside only.
Grow edible plants only in containers that held food or drink and in untreated wood.
never: Never reuse chemical, pesticide, solvent or motor-oil containers for food, drink, edible plants or pets.
Never store food in cracked or chipped containers.
